title: Cyclone Akvan weakens as it closes in on Gopalpur for landfall; Odisha moves over 3 lakh people
dek: The India Meteorological Department says the storm lost strength overnight and its landfall process near Gopalpur was due to begin on Friday morning. Heavy rain is forecast for Odisha and south Bengal through Saturday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclone Akvan weakened overnight from a severe cyclonic storm to a cyclonic storm and was about 110 km south of Gopalpur at 5.30 am on Friday, with its landfall process due to begin within about two hours, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said, as Odisha reported that it had moved more than 3 lakh people out of low-lying and vulnerable areas. The IMD expects the storm to cross the coast close to Gopalpur in Odisha's Ganjam district by Friday forenoon, with maximum sustained winds of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph.

That is weaker than the 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, that the IMD had forecast for landfall as late as Thursday night. But the department kept its red message for the north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts, and warned of extremely heavy rain of 21 cm or more at isolated places in Odisha on Friday, a storm surge of up to a metre in low-lying coastal districts, and a moderate risk of flash floods in parts of Odisha and south Bengal.

## What happened

In its latest national bulletin, the IMD said that at 5.30 am the storm lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal near the coast, about 70 km east of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 110 km south of Gopalpur, 170 km east-north-east of Visakhapatnam and 200 km south-south-west of Puri. It had sped up to 23 kmph over the previous six hours, moving north-north-west, compared with about 13 kmph on Thursday afternoon. Three hours earlier it had been 170 km south of Gopalpur.

Land interaction had begun as the storm's outer rain band moved over land, and "the landfall process will commence during next 2 hours", the bulletin said. The storm is being tracked by the Doppler weather radar at Gopalpur. Rain had been falling along the south Odisha coast since Thursday: Gopalpur recorded 166 mm by 4.30 am on Friday, according to reports, and heavy rain and gusty winds hit Bhubaneswar from about 1 am.

The IMD's forecast table has the storm weakening fast once it is over land: to a deep depression, with winds of 50-60 kmph, by 5.30 pm on Friday as it moves north over interior Odisha, and to a well-marked low-pressure area, with winds of 25-35 kmph, by 11.30 pm on Friday, earlier than the department had forecast a few hours before.

## Evacuation and preparations

Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed preparations at the Special Relief Commissioner's office in Bhubaneswar from about 11 pm on Thursday until about 1.30 am on Friday and directed officials to work towards a "zero-casualty" target, according to reports. After the review, the state said preparations covered 20 districts and that more than 3 lakh people had been moved, a figure that has risen through the week: 46,701 on Thursday morning and 1,05,304 by Thursday evening, according to Chief Secretary Anu Garg.

According to the figures released after the review, 4,170 pregnant women close to their due dates were moved to health facilities, of whom 1,317 have given birth. Of 9,341 cyclone shelters readied, 2,623 were in use. The state has deployed 418 teams: 60 of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, 14 of the National Disaster Response Force, 216 fire service teams and 128 tree-cutting teams of the Odisha Forest Development Corporation, with 28 more fire service teams on standby. Reports differ on the number of trains affected: East Coast Railway has cancelled several trains and rescheduled 26, and some reports put the total cancelled or rescheduled at about 50. Flights to and from Bhubaneswar, Visakhapatnam and Kolkata have also been affected, according to reports.

The Department of Telecommunications has switched on intra-circle roaming in six districts, Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha, until midnight on Friday, letting phones use any operator's network, according to the Odisha government. The state's water resources department has cut reservoir levels by about half and ruled out an immediate major flood, according to reports.

In Andhra Pradesh, the storm's turn to the north-north-west has eased concern, but the IMD still expects heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in north coastal Andhra on Friday, and reports said Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Parvathipuram Manyam could see extremely heavy falls.

## Warnings for Friday

- Rain: heavy to very heavy at a few places and extremely heavy (21 cm or more) at isolated places over Odisha on Friday, easing to heavy rain at isolated places over north Odisha on Saturday
- Flash floods: moderate risk over the next 24 hours in Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Baleshwar, Bhadrak, Cuttack, Dhenkanal, Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar and Jajpur in Odisha, and East Midnapore, Howrah, North and South 24 Parganas and Nadia in Bengal
- Storm surge: 0.5-1 metre above the astronomical tide in low-lying parts of Ganjam and Puri, and of Kakinada, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam in Andhra, at landfall
- Wind: gales of 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph along the south Odisha coast until Friday afternoon
- Fishermen: not to go into the north-west and west-central Bay of Bengal until Saturday morning

## Bengal

South Bengal is on the wetter side of the storm's track. The IMD expects heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on Friday and heavy rain on Saturday. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata has forecast 7-20 cm at one or two places in South 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura until 8.30 am on Saturday, and 7-11 cm in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas and Purulia. The Kolkata Municipal Corporation has put its control room on round-the-clock watch for waterlogging, fallen trees and damaged buildings and cancelled leave for drainage staff, according to reports. Squally winds of 50-60 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, are expected along the Bengal coast until Friday forenoon.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone of the post-monsoon season in the Bay of Bengal and the third to threaten the same stretch of coast in about four weeks, after Arnab in late October and Murasu at the start of November. Its forecast track shifted several times this week: the IMD moved the expected crossing south, to between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, by Tuesday evening, then back north to the Narsapur-Puri stretch on Wednesday, and lowered the expected strength at landfall more than once. The storm slowed to about 5 kmph on Wednesday night before speeding up towards the coast. Murasu, which crossed near Ongole on 3 November, damaged crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 Andhra districts, according to the state government. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said on Thursday that the exact landfall point and impact would depend on the storm's movement.

Odisha's evacuation-first approach dates from the 1999 super cyclone, which killed about 10,000 people in the state. Since then the state has built a network of cyclone and flood shelters and moves people to them before a storm arrives.

## What happens next

The IMD's next bulletins will confirm when and where landfall is complete, which is expected by late Friday morning. The heaviest rain is expected over Odisha through Friday, moving north into Jharkhand and south-west Bengal as the system weakens on Friday night and Saturday. Damage assessments, and decisions on when people can return home from shelters, will follow once the winds drop.
